environment.description: Same Go WebSocket service on ECS Fargate connecting to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 15. The database uses a restricted role `app_rls_user` which has `SET row_security = on` enforced via ALTER ROLE. Row-level security policies are FORCE-enabled on all tenant-scoped tables (events, users) with `ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. The RLS policy on each table is: `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON <table> USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant'))`. A connection-pool hook (pgbouncer transaction-mode with server_reset_query including `SET app.current_tenant = ''`) ensures session variables don't leak. However, note: the application code does NOT call `SET app.current_tenant` — instead, a PostgreSQL event trigger on the `pg_stat_activity` view combined with a custom `auth_hook` extension sets `app.current_tenant` based on the `application_name` connection parameter which is configured in the connection string as the tenant ID extracted by the sidecar proxy. The sidecar (Envoy with a custom Lua filter) rewrites the PostgreSQL startup message to inject the authenticated tenant_id into `application_name` before forwarding to pgbouncer.

config.db_role: app_rls_user (ALTER ROLE app_rls_user SET row_security = on)
config.rls_policies: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on events, users tables
config.rls_policy_definition: CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON events USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')); CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON users USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant'));
config.connection_pool: pgbouncer transaction-mode, server_reset_query = 'RESET ALL; SET app.current_tenant = '''
config.tenant_injection: Envoy sidecar Lua filter extracts tenant from mTLS SPIFFE ID, injects into PG startup application_name
config.auth_hook: pg_tle function on client_connection_check_hook sets app.current_tenant from application_name
config.network: NLB passthrough, service mesh with mTLS between sidecar and pgbouncer
